searchText: Just to note that blst rust bindings does some workflow in thread pool so when calculating gas this needs to ba taken into account. It will use clot `blst_p1s_mult_pippenger` only if `cpu_n < 2` https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/6f3136ffb636974166a93f2f25436854fe8d10ff/bindings/rust/src/pippenger.rs#L143 Do we have code that did this gas estimations, this could be very valuable? As we discussed with geth, we don't want a precompile to run on multiple threads. <@427903869226582018> <@360491619402776577> Agreeing on this, gas pricing should be made on single thread. Just making a note **if** benchmark for gas discount was made in rust and this feature was enabled we should revisit it. In deployment, would you be running it on multiple threads? Or is this just for gas benchmarks? Interested in what <@427903869226582018> , <@425274498732916736> and others are doing here Geth will run it with multiple threads. Whats the rationale for this? Versus running it on a single thread? just trying to figure out how folks are thinking about benchmarking on a single thread and then running on multiple threads There is no reason not to run in multiple threads The discrepancy between measuring on a single thread is fine then I’m guessing? I think for gas benchmarking: conceptually the EVM is a single thread of execution, and we want to keep the pricing tuned to not break that assumption. But clients are free to run it however they want to maximize performance. Yeah makes sense — do clients do this with other precompiles too? off the top of my head, I can't think of another existing precompile that benefits from multithreading Or perhaps there has not been a precompile big enough to warrant it? Okay I see I'm also against of considering multi-threading execution: 1. As already mentioned, since 10 years EVM is single-threaded. You should not suddenly and silently drop a thread-pool to it. 2. What is your baseline? 4, 16 or 256 threads? 3. You need a thread-pool in your EVM. This is complicated component with non-deterministic properties. You benchmark it in clean environment, but in production other CPUs may do something useful (e.g. networking, io, beacon chain client, db compacting, metrics). To clarify, when you deploy, you will be running the msm precompile on a single thread? Yes. We actually have no other option even for testing.

excerpts.author: jwasinger
excerpts.content:
I think for gas benchmarking:  conceptually the EVM is a single thread of execution, and we want to keep the pricing tuned to not break that assumption.

But clients are free to run it however they want to maximize performance.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content:
I'm also against of considering multi-threading execution:
1. As already mentioned, since 10 years EVM is single-threaded. You should not suddenly and silently drop a thread-pool to it.
2. What is your baseline? 4, 16 or 256 threads?
3. You need a thread-pool in your EVM. This is complicated component with non-deterministic properties. You benchmark it in clean environment, but in production other CPUs may do something useful (e.g. networking, io, beacon chain client, db compacting, metrics).
